rejection_findings.finding: The rewrite overstates the 236b phrasing as improvised and lacks accepted support for Menexenus permitting attribution to anyone.

revisions.title: A speech passed through layers
revisions.body: Before the oration begins, Socrates turns authorship into a chain of reports. He says he heard Aspasia deliver a funeral speech, one assembled from remnants of the speech Pericles had delivered. He disavows anything from himself, remembers learning it from Aspasia, and fears her anger if he brings it out. Menexenus then says he may tell it as Aspasia’s or anyone else’s. The speech starts under that layered uncertainty.
